code_observation: parallel_sync_101::overlap uses Builder::spawn_scoped for every publication. Removing repeated creation/join overhead is directly testable, regardless of whether it caused the failed tails.
hypothesis: One lazily created, owned, bounded synchronization worker per Archive can retain the overlap of both original sync_all operations with less repeated thread overhead, while completing every job before catalog rename and ACK.
proposed_protocol: Only an already completely written/flushed segment File is transferred to the worker; do not duplicate the OS handle or add unsafe lifetime tricks.
A zero-capacity private request channel and capacity-one completion channel admit at most one job. Archive's existing mutable writer access remains the serialization boundary.

Preserve Archive and ArchiveSnapshot Send/Sync traits with compile-time controls. A bare mpsc Receiver would remove Sync; use a private Mutex around it with get_mut under the existing exclusive writer access, or an equivalently bounded safe design.
The request and reply carry a checked monotonic ticket. The reply returns the same owned File and sync outcome only after all job work and hooks complete.
The parent prepares, writes and syncs the catalog concurrently, catches catalog unwind, and always waits for actual job completion. Both original sync_all calls stay mandatory.
Catalog rename, publication metadata changes, source checkpoints and ACK occur only after successful matching completion and successful catalog sync.

Any spawn, handoff, reply, ticket, sync or panic failure prevents rename/ACK and retains conservative unknown-outcome poisoning. Never silently fall back or report a disconnected worker as successful.

A worker owns an Arc of the existing exclusive lease. Its stop/drop closes admission and joins the actual thread before Archive can release its lease. Snapshots keep their existing lease/pin contract.

Do not retain a segment File or queued work after completing a reply. An idle worker may persist only for its owning Archive; no global pool, orphan thread, unbounded queue or work surviving owner shutdown.
Prefer a separate third publication function selected by a new opt-in feature, leaving the entire feature-disabled and 101 publication bodies byte-exact. Do not format or rewrite unrelated source.
Reuse the unchanged asynchronous reclaimer, ownership, pinning, format, receipt/source digest, queue budget, arrival/drain, client/dispatch and shutdown contracts. Add no dependency or version bump.
